shots.synced_phrase: To understand the couple ... Flanders
shots.narration_words: To understand the couple, we first have to understand their city. In the early fifteenth century, booming trade produced a new rung on the social ladder, a class of rich and powerful merchants, and nowhere were they more at home than Bruges, in Flanders, which is today part of northern Belgium.

Bruges was an international crossroads, where wool, spices, silk and furs arrived from every direction, and where ambitious people came from across the known world to make their fortunes. One of those families came from Lucca, in Tuscany, and was called Arnolfini.

shots.synced_phrase: As the merchants got richer
shots.narration_words: As the merchants got richer, their hunger for prestige grew with them, and the surest sign that you had arrived was to be painted, which in the 1430s meant being painted by one particular man.

shots.synced_phrase: So let us return ... so that we would know
shots.narration_words: So let us return to the question we started with. Is this a wedding portrait of a pregnant bride? Almost certainly not. It may record a marriage, it may be a memorial, and perhaps it is a little of both, but if we follow the clues the painter left us, the dog, the roundels, the candle, the dark clothes and the grip of a hand, it begins to look like something deeper, a portrait of a love that outlasts death. And the man who was there to witness it signed his name above the mirror, so that we would know.
